blindSummary:
This jurisdiction is an autonomous overseas constituent country within the realm of a distant metropolitan state. It recognises same-sex marriages performed under the metropolitan state's law; it has an active local LGBT community and a local Pride; but locally there is no marriage-equality legislation and no legal gender recognition.

The metropolitan state's evidence base is the legal starting point here; local deviations are recorded above and in the notes.
blindOutOfScope: Overseas constituent country of a distant metropolitan state; local deviations noted in the summary.
blindSourceSummaries: A safety and travel page from the host city of a recent international Pride event (its content is about the metropolitan state; included here because this jurisdiction is an autonomous constituent country of that state's overseas realm): border/airport procedures, entry rules of the metropolitan state's regional visa-free area, and a dedicated section for transgender and non-binary visitors.

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview of the metropolitan state (updated March 2026): progressive laws with gaps - legal gender change requires a medical expert letter; an 'X' marker is available only via a 3-9 month court procedure; the self-ID gender law was withdrawn in July 2025. This jurisdiction follows the realm-wide law with its own local framework.
Official tourism LGBT vacations page of a sister constituent country of the same realm (kingdom context for this jurisdiction): markets the region's islands as welcoming to all visitors.

Tourism-site news from a sister constituent country of the same realm: that island approved civil unions for same-sex couples, the first island in the region to do so - realm-wide context for this jurisdiction's own judicial recognition of same-sex marriage (2018).

Gay-travel news archive (2017): a feature on gay life in a tolerant island society - describes the three geographically nearest islands of this corner of the realm as quiet pockets of gay-friendliness, tolerant and mostly open.

Regional LGBT network report (April 2015), headlined to the effect that gay rights should arrive quickly in all parts of the realm: government representatives of all parts of the kingdom agreed that LGBT people across the realm's three overseas constituent countries should quickly receive equal rights; a package of demands was presented to the realm's seat of government; documents this jurisdiction's Pride-permit difficulties (2013) and the local government's stated support despite parliamentary opposition.
